description: DB-specific column -> (quantity_type, unit) mapping owned by SiennaGridDB. Consumed by scripts/generate_unit_registry.py together with SiennaSchemas Core/units.json (the vocabulary source of truth) to seed the unit_conventions table. Every (quantity_type, unit) here must exist in units.json allowed_units. Rows may carry an optional discriminator_column/discriminator_value pair, and an optional second discriminator_column_2/discriminator_value_2, for columns whose unit depends on one or two sibling columns (e.g. hydro_reservoirs.level_data_type). Basis is one such pair, standardized to a single discriminator_column value 'unit_basis' with two discriminator_value options: 'NATURAL_UNITS' (a physical unit -- ohm, S, MW, MVAr, kV -- self-contained, no base needed) or 'COMPONENT_BASE' (dimensionless pu against a base reachable from the row). quantity_type is the orthogonal second axis: under NATURAL_UNITS it also selects which physical representation a column holds, which is how a device's admittance is expressed either as Susceptance/S or Conductance/S (the electrical form) or as ReactivePower/MVAr or ActivePower/MW (the PSS/E form, at 1.0 pu voltage) on fixed_admittance/switched_admittance -- both NATURAL_UNITS, distinguished only by quantity_type. That is why the UNIQUE key on unit_conventions is (table_name, column_name, discriminator_value, discriminator_value_2, quantity_type), wide enough for two NATURAL_UNITS rows on one column, and why the no-discriminator partial index is keyed the same way. Every convention row whose unit is 'pu' carries base_power_ref and/or base_voltage_ref, naming which base(s) the value is normalized against; both are absent (never null) on non-pu rows. A bare column name means same-row; a '->' path is an FK hop, each segment after the first written as table.column, with the final segment naming the base column itself -- e.g. 'circuit->transformer_circuits.base_power', 'arc_id->arcs.from_id->balancing_topologies.base_voltage'. Voltage-quantity pu rows carry only base_voltage_ref; Resistance/Reactance/Susceptance/Conductance pu rows carry both, since the base impedance is base_voltage^2/base_power. The attributes.* rows are attribute-name conventions, not physical columns, and their pu rows (magnitude, voltage_limits) are exempt from base refs: the owner is polymorphic (entity_id -> entities), so no single static path applies, and they carry their own inline unit/quantity_type instead. Cost JSON blobs are registered as JSON-path column names (operation_cost.fixed, ...); a variable-cost curve's quantity depends on the curve form the payload declares, so those rows discriminate on JSON paths inside the same blob (operation_cost.<curve>.value_curve.curve_type, and variable_cost_type where the schema permits a FuelCurve) rather than on a sibling column -- an INPUT_OUTPUT curve's y coordinate is a cost rate (USD/h) while INCREMENTAL and AVERAGE_RATE curves are per-energy (USD/MWh), and a FuelCurve's y is a heat rate.
